decisions.quote: In a pre-registered experiment (N = 313), we successfully replicated an experiment from Spranca, Minsk, and Baron (1991), considered a classic demonstration of the omission bias, examining generalizability to a between-subject design with extensions examining causality, intent, and regret.
decisions.reason: The authors state an explicit overall verdict that they successfully replicated the experiment from Spranca, Minsk, and Baron (1991) on its focal omission-bias contrast (morality and responsibility), while noting in the pre-registration and results that the secondary outcome-bias contrast was included for informational purposes and had mixed results in the original study as well.

decisions.quote: The classic action-effect (Kahneman & Tversky, 1982) findings were that actions leading to a negative outcome are regretted more than inactions leading to the same negative outcomes. We added a regret measure to examine whether the action-effect findings would extend to situations of morality involving intended harmful behavior.
decisions.reason: Kahneman and Tversky (1982) is cited as background literature on the action-effect to motivate adding a novel regret extension measure to the moral scenarios from Spranca et al. (1991), rather than as an original study directly re-tested by this replication.
